assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and its translation into incretin therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity is a rare case of basic hormone biology leading to a transformative, widely used therapy class with large clinical and societal impact. The discovery chain (proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36), mechanism of action, then stable agonists) is clear and conceptually original.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of the incretin effect and GLP-1 secretion and action) and Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology, GLP-1 and GLP-2 receptor biology and clinical translation) are central. Mojsov's contribution on the active peptide form is real but contested in priority; Knudsen's drug development is decisive for the therapy but is industrial work that may fit less naturally than the discovery side. A three-person prize is possible but the credit balance is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple independent large clinical trials and outcome studies across diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular disease; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, with the clinical impact still unfolding.
uncertainties: Priority dispute around the active GLP-1 peptide form and the role of Habener, who is not in the credited list.
Whether the committee would weigh peptide-drug development (Knudsen) alongside the physiology.
Long-term safety and outcome data are still accumulating; my recollection of details is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling logic in which the endoplasmic reticulum reports its folding state to the nucleus, with the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 splicing mechanism being unusually elegant, including unconventional cytoplasmic mRNA splicing. It underpins understanding of proteostasis, secretory cell physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter (IRE1, HAC1 mRNA splicing, ISRIB and the pathway logic) and Mori (UPR element and transcriptional response, ATF6 and later work) are the clear pair. The supplied names support a clean two-person configuration. I treat both as decisive and recall, without independent verification, that they share major prior recognition.
assessment.maturity: Fundamental mechanism has been replicated and extended for over two decades in yeast and mammals. Disease-relevance and therapeutic translation is still maturing, but the basic discovery is mature and fit for recognition.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation (for example ISRIB, PERK and IRE1 modulators) is not yet established.
Other contributors to mammalian UPR branches (for example Ron, Harding, Walter's lab alumni) are not in the supplied credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines established prevention of a virus-caused cancer, with demonstrated reductions in persistent infection, cervical precancer and now invasive cervical cancer in vaccinated cohorts. Very high public-health impact and clear originality in using self-assembling L1 particles.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP assembly, immunogenicity) and Frazer (with the late Jian Zhou, who cannot be recognised, on L1/L2 VLP formation) form the plausible laureates. The Zhou issue and the parallel work by other groups complicate allocation, but the supplied three names support a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data from several countries over more than fifteen years are strong and independently confirmed; the recognition is timely. Zur Hausen already received a prize for the HPV-cancer link, which lowers novelty somewhat.
uncertainties: Posthumous exclusion of Jian Zhou and competing priority claims.
Whether the committee views vaccine development as less prize-eligible than the underlying discovery already honoured in 2008.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells have created a new class of living drugs, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemia and lymphoma and now moving into autoimmune disease. The concept of redirecting T cells with chimeric receptors with costimulation is original and has changed oncology practice.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain are the clearest on the engineered receptor and costimulatory design and the first clinical translation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. The original chimeric receptor concept of Eshhar is not on the supplied list, which complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products with years of follow-up confirm durable benefit in haematological malignancy; efficacy in solid tumours is limited. Timely, though the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: Eshhar and others' early contribution is not within the supplied names.
Toxicity (cytokine release, secondary malignancy signals) and limited solid-tumour efficacy.
Whether the immunotherapy theme is judged too close to the recent immune-related prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with millisecond precision, transforming circuit physiology and enabling studies across systems. The tool is among the most influential methods of the last two decades, though its impact is mainly as a research tool rather than a clinical therapy so far.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main obstacle: Bamberg, Nagel and Hegemann discovered and characterised channelrhodopsin, while Boyden and Deisseroth demonstrated neuronal expression and control, and Miesenböck pioneered earlier genetically encoded light-sensitisation. Only three names can be chosen; I favour the neuronal-application trio, but a prize excluding the channelrhodopsin discoverers would be hard to defend.
assessment.maturity: Very widely validated and used for over fifteen years; mature as a method, with first clinical applications (retinal vision restoration) emerging.
uncertainties: Genuinely unresolved allocation between the photoreceptor discoverers and the neuronal-application pioneers.
Limited direct medical translation to date.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishment of long-lived, self-organising adult stem-cell-derived organoids (from the Lgr5 stem-cell work through intestinal and then many epithelial organoids) created a general platform for human tissue modelling, disease and drug studies, and personalised medicine, with strong conceptual foundation in stem-cell niche biology.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual leader (Lgr5 stem cells, organoid culture conditions); Sato was first author on the key intestinal organoid paper. A two-person configuration is supported by the supplied credit, though Lgr5 stem-cell identification is a related but separate contribution.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced across many labs and tissues with clinical use as a screening tool beginning (for example cystic fibrosis drug testing); the platform is mature, though the clinical impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Compound discovery (Lgr5 stem cells versus organoid culture) may need distinct recognition and other contributors such as Clevers' collaborators or Wnt-pathway workers.
Predictive clinical value of organoids is still being demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and elucidation of mTOR signalling established a central growth and nutrient-sensing control node with major implications for metabolism, ageing, cancer, immunology and neurobiology. The conceptual importance is high.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast, which is the decisive step. Schreiber's chemical-biology work (FKBP12-rapamycin) and Sabatini's mTOR complex and nutrient-sensing work are important but the central credit probably belongs primarily to Hall and perhaps one of the mammalian pioneers; Sabatini's standing may also be affected by non-scientific considerations that I cannot verify and do not rely on.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed extensively for three decades; rapalogs are in clinical use for transplantation and oncology, though broad therapeutic expectations (for example ageing) remain unproven.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and other mammalian TOR pioneers (Sabatini, Abraham, Sabers) is unresolved.
Complex-level biology is still evolving, so the interpretation continues to be refined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of cell-free fetal DNA in maternal plasma opened noninvasive prenatal testing, now used for millions of pregnancies, and the methodology generalised to liquid biopsy for cancer. Original, clear and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: Lo is the discoverer and the principal developer of the clinical applications, giving a clean single-laureate configuration; commercial development by others is incremental relative to the founding discovery.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed and widely implemented over more than a decade; recognition would be timely. Clinical scope still expanding in oncology.
uncertainties: Single-laureate prizes are rarer, and the committee may prefer a broader discovery.
Diagnostic technology rather than mechanism of disease, which may weigh against it relative to physiological discoveries.
